# shed's methods in a script

<!-- Generated from crates/shed-proto by `just generate`; do not edit. -->

Call one as `shed.<method>(params)`; `shed.describe("<method>")` gives its params and result.
A `read` is called as it is, a `guarded` one goes through the server's guard first (refused with none), and a `refused` one is a `ShedError` `NOT_IN_SCRIPT`.

| Method | In a script | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account.add` | guarded | Make an account: an empty config folder of mode 0700 under `accounts/<provider>/<name>`, or with `folder` a link to that existing folder, adopted in place; a folder holding one of the record's `setup_files` is refused (`ACCOUNT_SETUP`). `token_file`, a file of mode 0600 on this host, is copied in as the account's setup token. The same call twice is one account. |
| `account.login` | refused | The record's `login` in a redacted terminal `login-<provider>-<name>` with the account's folder set; a second call while it runs returns the same terminal. shed kills it after 600 s; when it ends shed runs `account.status`. With `token`, the record's `token.command` runs instead, and shed saves the setup token it prints, read off the unredacted screen, to the account's 0600 token file. |
| `account.ls` | guarded | The accounts, per provider `default` first, then in the order `auto` picks: what shed last read of each, its token's dates (never the token), the setup files its folder holds and the terminals on it. A reading older than the record's `usage.fresh` is read again in the background. |
| `account.rm` | guarded | The record's `logout`, then the account's folder (an adopted one: only its link), its token and its readings; refused for `default` and while its login runs. |
| `account.status` | guarded | Run the record's status command and usage probe for the account now, and keep what they say. |
| `account.use` | guarded | Make a named, ready account the provider's preferred one, which `auto` picks first while it is ready and not limited, and move every live ACP or stream lane of the provider on `auto` or `default` to it: the lane stops its agent (a busy one once its tool call ends), copies the session's `session_files` and loads the session on the account, now on `auto`; a lane that was mid-turn or rate-limited gets one prompt to go on. Refused for `default`, an unknown, signed-out, limited or set-up account. Without `name` it only drops the preference. |
| `acp.model` | guarded | Switch an ACP terminal's model to one of its `session.models`: its bridge asks the agent (`session/set_config_option`, the `model` option) and emits `session` with the new `model`. |
| `agents` | read | Each agent shed has a provider record for or has installed, by id, as `shed agents --json` prints it: the record (its limit and login-expired lines, hooks and program facts), its `source` (`built-in` or the user file in `<config>/providers/` that adds or overrides it) and the installed adapter. A bad user file is skipped (`shed doctor` names it). |
| `agents.match` | read | Apply agent `id`'s limit and auth rules to `text` (a pane's screen, a reply): the first line that says a usage limit was hit with its reset time, and the first that says the login expired, as an ACP lane would read them. An agent with no record matches nothing. |
| `attach` | refused | Take over the terminal. After the response the server writes a redraw (clear, then the screen text) and the program's raw output, and closes the connection when the program's PTY closes. The client sends only notifications from then on (`terminal.input`, `keys`, `resize`); detaching is closing the connection. |
| `code.find` | guarded | The files under `root` that best answer `query`'s words, best first: the top 10 (`top`, at most 50) of a stated `total`. A word earns points in a file's name, its folders, its symbols' names and its lines; the sum is multiplied by the words that earned any and halved for a test. Each file names its score, short `why` reasons and the symbols that earned them. The walk and its limits are `code.grep`'s. `machine` searches there. |
| `code.grep` | guarded | The lines under `root` that match, grouped by the symbols around them, in name order. The walk keeps to `.gitignore` and `info/exclude`, skips `.git`, dot names without `hidden`, symlinks and binary files. A line over 4,096 bytes comes back `clipped` with its `length`. Over 20,000 files, 250 rows, 256 MiB or 10 s is `LIMIT`. `machine` searches there. |
| `code.outline` | guarded | A file's functions, types, sections and blocks in file order, each with its kind, name, lines and depth, by line rules for Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Markdown and TOML and by indentation for other files. Over 2,000 symbols or 256 MiB is `LIMIT`. `machine` reads it there. |
| `emit` | refused | Emit one of an ACP terminal's structured events (`turn`, `text`, `tool_call`, `plan`, `mode`, `approval_request`, `approved`, `reply`); its bridge (`shed run --acp`) calls this. Other events are refused. |
| `events` | refused | Stream events. After the response the server writes one event per line (see Events) for the terminals carrying every one of `labels`, first those after `since` still kept (the last 4,096 events, and each terminal's last 256 `text` chunks before them), and never closes the connection; closing it unsubscribes. When events after `since` are gone it first writes `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"reset","params":{"seq":N}}`: those up to `N` are lost. A client more than 4,096 events behind gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"lagged","params":{"seq":N}}` and the connection is closed; it resumes with `since`. A connection that sent `heartbeat` gets `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"heartbeat"}` lines when idle. |
| `exec` | guarded | Run a program without a terminal in a process group of its own, `stdin` fed to it and `env` over the server's variables (kept in memory only), and answer with its exit code (128 + the signal when one ended it) and the exact bytes it wrote. The group is ended when the program returns or `timeout` seconds pass (`IO`); output over `REPLY_LIMIT` bytes is `IO`, never cut. `machine` runs it there, over the held link. `sandbox` runs it inside `srt` with those rules, as `run`'s does (`docs/hosts/sandbox.md`). |
| `file.read` | guarded | A file's bytes, or with `lines` only that span's; over `REPLY_LIMIT` bytes is `IO`. `machine` reads it there. |
| `file.write` | guarded | Replace a file with `data`: written to a temp file beside it, then renamed over it, its mode kept, or `mode` when given (the temp file has it before any byte is written). `machine` writes it there. |
| `flow.report` | read | Each flow's table as it ran beside today's code (#309): its mode, the subjects it tracks, how often each row fired, the facts it never took, the `never` rows that fired and the `stuck` reasons, all kept in `flow-counts.json` since they were first kept; and the lines of `flow-shadow.jsonl` from `since` on (default the last 7 days), by class: `state` when the table and today's code showed different states for more than 2 s, `action` when the table's row would have acted and today's code did not. `machine` asks that machine, over its held link. |
| `get` | read | One terminal. |
| `handover` | refused | Hand over to the binary the server was started from, which must be `build`: after the same check as `handover.check` it answers, waits up to 10 s for the other requests in flight, then replaces itself in place on the same process id, keeping the socket and every running terminal (screen, children and exit statuses). Every connection is closed: a closed connection means reconnect and ask again; `events` with `since` gets `reset`. A refused or failed handover leaves the server serving as it was. |
| `handover.check` | refused | Would the server hand over to the binary at `candidate`: it runs `<candidate> serve --preflight`, which must name `build`, read the state file and inherit this server's handover format, and speak the protocol of every live ACP bridge. Changes nothing; `HANDOVER_REFUSED` says why not. |
| `heartbeat` | refused | Keep the connection alive. Once a connection sends one, the server closes it when nothing comes from it for 30 s (two missed beats of 15 s), and writes a `heartbeat` line every 15 s into its idle `events` stream. A write the client does not take within 30 s also closes any connection. |
| `hello` | refused | The handshake; must come first on every connection. Another product, or a protocol range that does not overlap the server's, is refused with `SHED_VERSION`. |
| `install.back` | refused | Renames `<dest>.prev` over the live binary, once `<dest>.prev --version` answers; else `UNSTAGED` and nothing moves. Only shed's own binary or the client's tool, else `NOT_OWN_BINARY`. |
| `install.find` | refused | A release's `SHA256SUMS`, read on the main host; none there yet is `NO_RELEASE`. `tool` must be `shed` or the tool the client named at `hello`, else `NOT_OWN_BINARY`. |
| `install.ls` | refused | The `--version` line of `<dest>`, `<dest>.new` and `<dest>.prev`. `dest` must be shed's own binary or the tool's the client named at `hello`, else `NOT_OWN_BINARY`. |
| `install.stage` | refused | Downloads `<tool>-<arch>-<os>` to `<dest>.new.part`, checks its sha256 against `SHA256SUMS`, makes it 755, checks that its `--version` contains `build` and renames it to `<dest>.new`; the live binary is untouched. A failed check removes the file and is `UNSTAGED`, naming it (`asset`, `download`, `checksum`, `version`); `build` already staged fetches nothing. Only shed's own binary or the client's tool, else `NOT_OWN_BINARY`. |
| `install.swap` | refused | Keeps the live binary as `<dest>.prev` (a hard link) and renames `<dest>.new` over it, once `<dest>.new --version` answers with `build`; else `UNSTAGED` and nothing moves. Live already `build`: nothing. Only shed's own binary or the client's tool, else `NOT_OWN_BINARY`. |
| `keys` | guarded | Press keys by name (`enter`, `esc`, `ctrl+c`, `up`, …); nothing is sent if any name is unknown. |
| `kill` | guarded | End the terminal's whole process tree (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); returns the exited terminal. |
| `ls` | read | List terminals, by name; `labels` keeps those that carry every given label, `parent` the children of that terminal. |
| `machine.add` | guarded | Add a machine to the config file, as `shed machine add` does, and start holding its link; the same name and target again is the same machine, another target under a taken name `INVALID_PARAMS`. |
| `machine.links` | read | Each configured machine's held link: `up`, `reconnecting` or `down`, since when, why it is down, and `down_since`, when it last left `up` (or was first tried; a retry does not move it); once up, the shed there (`hello`) and the machine's `os`, `arch` and `home`. A request naming `<machine>/<name>` (`get`, `read`, `send`, `keys`, `kill`, `rm`, `state`, `acp.model`, `terminal.procs`, `wait`; `run` with `machine`, ACP ones bridged by that server) goes over the link; `ls` and `events` include every machine, their names so prefixed. Reads the config again, linking machines added since. |
| `machine.rm` | guarded | Remove a machine from the config file, as `shed machine rm` does, and drop its held link; removing one that is not there is a no-op. |
| `machine.stats` | read | The machine's health now: load per CPU, memory pressure (percent of memory not available, and on macOS the kernel's level `mem_level`: `normal`, `warn` or `critical`), free and total memory, swap used and pages swapped out since boot, free and total space on the volume of the state file, CPUs, uptime and the terminals by state (the reported state while running, else `running`; `exited`). The server keeps one sample a minute for 24 h; `since` (unix seconds) adds those after it as `history`. `top` adds that many processes using the most CPU (`top_cpu`) and the most memory (`top_mem`), each naming the terminal whose tree holds it; `machine` asks that machine, over its held link. |
| `proxy.keys` | guarded | The token proxy's per-run keys, newest first: each one's id, terminal, account and state; never a key. |
| `proxy.relay` | refused | Server to server, over a held link: this machine's loopback relay port, kept for good, and a fresh socket path the main host's next forward binds; the relay passes bytes to it and holds no key or token. |
| `proxy.revoke` | guarded | The key stops signing at once; an unknown id is `INVALID_PARAMS`. |
| `read` | read | The visible screen, or with `history` the scrollback and screen, as plain text; `lines` keeps the last N lines. Every read returns a `cursor`; with `since: <cursor>` only what is new: the lines that scrolled off since (`lost: N` when scrollback dropped N of them first), then the screen only when it changed (`changed`), so nothing new is an empty `text`. ACP: the transcript as text, or with `events` its events (each with its `seq`), paged by `before` and `n`, or with `since` only those after its `seq`. |
| `resize` | guarded | Resize the terminal; the program gets SIGWINCH. |
| `rm` | guarded | Remove an exited terminal, its ACP session closed; returns it as it was. |
| `rpc.discover` | read | The whole API as one OpenRPC document, as `shed schema` prints it (`docs/shed.openrpc.json`): every method's params and result, the streamed events and screen updates, and the error codes, as JSON Schema. Needs no `hello`. |
| `run` | guarded | Start a terminal. `name` defaults to the first free `tN`; `keep` brings it back as a shell in its cwd after a server restart; `rows` and `cols` default to `$SHED_SIZE` (`RxC`) of the server, else 50x200. ACP: `mcp_servers` (stdio, `http`, `sse`, in ACP's shapes) go to the agent; their env and header values are never saved or shown. `meta` (an object) goes unchanged as the session's `_meta`. `no_hibernate` keeps the agent running when idle. `mem_max_mb` (default the server's `$SHED_MEM_MAX`, e.g. `4G`) limits the process tree's memory, and a `mem-limit` event (with `notify`, a `[shed] <name> mem-limit …` line to the parent) says what was ended: on Linux with a user systemd that has the memory controller the program runs in its own scope with `MemoryMax` and the kernel ends a process (the agent's children are ranked first); elsewhere, once the tree is over for two samples in a row, the sampler ends the largest process the agent started (SIGTERM, SIGKILL 2 s later), and an agent over it by itself is only reported. The sampler is a guard against sustained use, not a hard limit: a fast allocation can pass it between samples. `warm` takes the ready spare session of the same recipe (agent, command, cwd, policy, MCP servers, meta, size), renamed to `name` with these labels, and starts the next spare; spares are listed as `.warm-N`, at most `$SHED_WARM_MAX` (default 2) of them, each killed after `$SHED_WARM_IDLE` seconds (default 600) unused. `parent` links it to the terminal that started it: when the parent's program ends the child is killed too, unless `outlive`; with `notify` a `[shed] <name> blocked\|error\|exited …` line is typed into the parent (a prompt for an ACP parent) when the child blocks, errors or ends, once per piece of news, held while the parent reports `working`. `account` (ACP, on the main host) runs the agent on that account of its provider (`account.ls`): its folder variable set, its token too while its own login is signed out, none of the record's `scrub` and `cache.api_vars` inherited, and a caller `env` setting any of them refused; `meta` and the command are unchanged, and the token is kept in memory only. `policy` `judge` (ACP) runs `judge` (argv) in the terminal's cwd for each permission request, with one JSON object on its stdin: `name`, `labels`, `cwd`, `tool_call` (the agent's ACP `toolCall`: `kind`, `title`, `rawInput`, `locations`, …; `null` when it sent none) and `options` (each `id`, `name`, `kind`); it answers on stdout with `{"decision": "allow" \| "deny", "reason": "…"}`. `allow` picks the first `allow_once` option, else `allow_always`, so a later call still reaches the judge; `deny` picks the first `reject_once`, else `reject_always`; with no such option the request is cancelled. It fails closed: a judge that does not start, exits non-zero, takes over `judge_secs` (default 30) or prints no verdict is a `deny` with that reason. The `approved` event records `by: judge`, the `decision` and the `reason`. `sandbox` runs the program (ACP: the agent, each time the bridge starts it) inside `srt` with rules shed writes on that machine: the caller's `read`, `write`, `deny`, `hosts`, `sockets` and `mach`, the agent record's `[sandbox]`, and shed's own denies; a `write` that holds shed's state, its config or the folder `srt` or shed is in is `INVALID_PARAMS`, `keep` or `warm` with it is `INVALID_PARAMS`, and no `srt` there is `SANDBOX_MISSING` (`docs/hosts/sandbox.md`). |
| `screen.watch` | refused | Stream a running terminal's screen. After the response the server writes screen updates (see Screen updates), at most 20 a second: the full screen first (none when `since` is the screen's current `seq`), then the rows that changed. It closes the connection when the program's PTY closes. The connection still takes requests; their responses are not written. |
| `script` | refused | Run a program in shed's JavaScript subset (the body of an async function, at most 256 KiB) beside the terminals: `shed.<method>(params)` calls a method by its wire name through the same path a request takes, and what the program returns is `result`. A read (`ls`, `get`, `read`, `wait`, `machine.stats`, `machine.links`, `agents`, `agents.match`, `rpc.discover`, `terminal.procs`) is called as it is; any other method that acts is first shown to the guard of `[script]` in the server's config file (one process for the run, one JSON line each way per call, or with `guard_per = "call"` a process per call), and with none configured it is refused; streams, a person's input and the connection's own methods are refused (`NOT_IN_SCRIPT`). `caller` goes to the guard unchanged. Steps, live memory, calls, logs and the deadline (`timeout`, 60 s, at most 600) bound a run. The reply is `{result, logs, calls, acting, ms}` or, when the program failed, `{error, …}`; `acting` lists every guarded call with its params and its result or error. With `check` it is parsed and compiled only. Closing the connection cancels the calls in flight; `machine` runs it there, over the held link. |
| `secret.ls` | guarded | shed's own secrets by name, with when each was saved; never a value. |
| `secret.rm` | guarded | Removes one of shed's own secrets; twice is once. |
| `secret.set` | refused | Saves one of shed's own secrets (a VM provider's key) on the main host: a Keychain item on macOS, a 0600 file elsewhere. The value is never logged, saved in the state file or returned. |
| `send` | guarded | Paste text into the terminal, then press enter: bracketed when the program has turned bracketed paste on, unless `no_paste`; no enter with `no_enter`. While a person has an unsent line (typed through `terminal.input`), the send waits until they press enter or clear it (`ctrl+u`, `ctrl+c`), or `DRAFT_HELD` once `draft_wait` seconds (default 60, 0 off) pass after their last key, writing nothing. Sends go in one at a time, each whole. ACP: the text goes to the bridge as it is. |
| `state` | guarded | Report the terminal's state (`working`, `blocked`, `done` or `error`) with an optional note; a program can also print `ESC ] 7501 ; state=<s>[;note=<n>] BEL`, which never reaches the screen. The terminal also speaks the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501, revision 0.4): `state=<s>[:<key>=<value>]…` with `idle` and `clear`, `id`, `kind`, `progress`, `app` and base64 `title` and `msg`, and answers the probe `ESC ] 7501 ; ?`. A report with an `id` is a record of its own (`records`); on exit `working` and `blocked` ones are dropped. |
| `terminal.input` | refused | Type text into the terminal as a person: written as it is, and a line left unsent holds `send`s until enter, `ctrl+u` or `ctrl+c`. |
| `terminal.keys` | refused | Press keys by name as a person, as `keys`; `ctrl-x` is `ctrl+x`. Like `terminal.input`, a line left unsent holds `send`s. |
| `terminal.procs` | read | The terminal's live process tree, parents first, each with its `depth` below the terminal's own process, its CPU (percent of one core over its life, and `cpu_ms`, its CPU time, whose difference over two reads is a share), memory, age and command line; `own` marks the agent's own processes, not work it started. A terminal that is not running has none. |
| `terminal.readonly` | refused | Mark the terminal read-only for this connection: from then on, until it closes, the connection's `send`, `keys`, `resize`, `attach`, `terminal.input`, `terminal.keys` and `terminal.resize` to the terminal are refused with `READONLY`. The connection may resize only the terminals it has not marked. |
| `terminal.resize` | refused | Resize the terminal, as `resize`; without `terminal`, the one this connection watches. |
| `wait` | read | Answer once the reported state is one of `until` (`idle` too, from the `idle_after` fallback; `blocked` only of `kind`, if given) or a visible screen line matches the pattern `output` (`matched`), the program exits (`exited`) or `timeout` seconds pass (`timeout`). The server blocks; nothing polls. With `children`, `name` is a parent: `all` matches once no child is working (`terminal` is the parent), `any` on the next child that reports `done`, `blocked` or `error`, or exits (`terminal` is that child; `exited` when no child runs). |
